clue.text: Cheek from defensive player about bowler, for example

blocks.note: in football or rugby a back is a defender
C is short for circa, Latin for about
a bowler is a type of hat

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder gives lip to the bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: In the cricket picture the bowler is the player delivering the ball; here it is the round felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Backchat is insolent answering back, which is the same thing as cheek in its sense of impudent talk.

clue.text: British tree with less on top

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
the alder is a tree of damp ground

explanation.surface: A British tree that has lost some of its crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less on top' looks like a thinning tree canopy; it means less hair on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Balder is the comparative of bald: someone balder has less hair on the top of their head.

clue.text: Sign of growth to the south of island off Italy

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece to the south of another is written below it

blocks.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
corn is a crop, or a hard growth on the foot

explanation.surface: An indication of crops growing south of an Italian island.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn, the goat, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Lower score

blocks.note: first meaning: to reduce, as with prices
second meaning: to mark with a groove or incision

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a sports result; both words are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut prices is to reduce them, and to cut a surface is to make a scored line in it.

clue.text: Praise Catholic priest during hostilities

indicators.note: something happening during an event falls within it, so these pieces are placed inside

blocks.note: action means fighting
C is the abbreviation for Catholic
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: A Catholic priest is commended for conduct during wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface priest seems to belong with the Catholic, but it is a Buddhist lama.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclamation is loud, enthusiastic approval, a form of praise.

clue.text: Child aboard very old snowmobile

indicators.note: someone aboard is inside a vessel, so this word sits within another

blocks.note: so as in 'so good' means very
a kid is a child
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A youngster rides an ancient snow vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The child goes inside the word for very, and the abbreviation for old follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Skidoo is a trademark for a motorised sledge that has become a generic name for any snowmobile.

clue.text: Remain brief, and don't reveal one's thoughts

blocks.note: to keep is to stay or remain, as in 'keep calm'
a brief is a barrister, and so is counsel

explanation.surface: Be concise and keep your opinions to yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective meaning short; it is the British legal slang for a barrister, also called counsel.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep one's counsel is an idiom for keeping one's opinions or plans secret.

clue.text: Old coin adult found in passage

indicators.note: something found in a place is located inside it

blocks.note: a duct is a tube or channel
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up discovers an antique coin in a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: The ducat was a gold or silver coin used across Europe for centuries, so an old coin.

clue.text: Facing one's counterpart on location

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: informal British word for a colleague or partner
a site is a location

explanation.surface: Coming face to face with your opposite number on site.
explanation.walkthrough: Oppo is informal British English for a partner or opposite number.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite, as an adjective or preposition, means directly across from and facing something.

clue.text: Work on cheek with second cosmetic

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing on another is written after it

blocks.note: lip means impudence, like cheek
S is the abbreviation for second
to tick is to work or function, as a clock does

explanation.surface: Applying make-up to the face with a second product.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests blusher on the cheek, but cheek here means insolence. The working word comes last because it sits on the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipstick is a coloured cosmetic applied to the lips, so it is one example of a cosmetic.

clue.text: Embarrassed top MP

blocks.note: an embarrassed person goes red
a cap is a top or lid

explanation.surface: A senior Member of Parliament is left red-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: MP looks like Member of Parliament, but here it is military police; redcap is British slang for a military policeman, from the red cap cover they wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcap is a British nickname for a member of the military police, an MP in that other sense.

clue.text: Order in Japanese dictionaries

indicators.note: the letters needed are found inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An instruction found in Japanese reference books.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree or command, so it is an order issued by authority.

clue.text: Book at that time peaked (a novel)

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

blocks.note: then means at that time
these seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A book whose popularity peaked then — a novel, as it happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like it describes the book, but it signals the anagram; the book is non-fiction, by zoologist Desmond Morris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Naked Ape is Desmond Morris's 1967 book on human behaviour seen through zoology.

clue.text: Stands down, putting seaman in charge during engagements

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits within it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
dates are social engagements
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A captain resigns after giving a sailor command amid battles.
explanation.walkthrough: Engagements suggests battles or betrothals, but it means appointments. The command abbreviation goes after the first letter of those appointments.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who abdicates gives up the throne, which is to stand down from office.

clue.text: Brought about, as if by magic?

blocks.note: first meaning: achieved the desired result
second, playful meaning: performed a conjuror's illusion

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second meaning as whimsical: taken literally, the everyday idiom describes a magician at work.
explanation.definitionFit: To do the trick is an idiom for achieving the desired result, and literally it is what a conjuror performs on stage.

clue.text: Male injured too, unfortunately, in play

indicators.note: something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters before it come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: all fourteen letters are used

explanation.surface: A man hurt in a stage production, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: Fitting for a tragedy in which the male lead also dies.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo and Juliet is Shakespeare's tragedy of two young lovers, so it is a play.

clue.text: Travel from place to place in Italy with nervous trainee

indicators.note: a nervous person is jittery and unsettled, so the letters are shaken up

blocks.note: IT is the abbreviation for Italy
these seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An anxious apprentice touring around Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: To itinerate is to go on a circuit or journey from one place to another, as a travelling preacher does.

clue.text: Expert on drink has a breakdown

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: crack as in 'crack shot' means expert
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A skilled person who drinks ends up collapsing.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack up is to suffer a mental or emotional collapse, which is what having a breakdown means.

clue.text: Is in charge of a disciplined organisation in Hastings - Ruth, I suspect, ahead of Penny

definitions.text: Is in charge of a disciplined organisation

indicators.note: a suspect account is doubtful and not straight, so the letters are not in their proper order
one thing ahead of another is written before it

blocks.note: the town and the name taken letter for letter
the pronoun, as written; it is also part of the anagram
P is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: Ruth, a strict manager in the Sussex town of Hastings, is suspected of something before Penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' joins the anagram fodder as well as reading as 'I suspect'. Hastings is a seaside town in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a tight ship is an idiom for managing an organisation with firm discipline and efficiency.

clue.text: Irritated husband in coffee shop, then daughter

indicators.note: something in a place sits inside it, so this letter goes within the next word

blocks.note: a café is a coffee shop
H is the abbreviation for husband
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A man gets annoyed at the café, and next his daughter does.
explanation.definitionFit: Chafed means rubbed sore, and figuratively annoyed or irritated.

clue.text: Edible fruit in cask we brought back - money's needed upfront?

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the letters are read from the end
something needed upfront goes at the very front of the word

blocks.note: cash is money
a tun is a large cask for wine or beer
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nuts stored in a barrel we carried home, with payment demanded in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cask' reads as a plain word in the surface, but it is a clue to the barrel name, joined with 'we' and then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: The cashew is the kidney-shaped seed of a tropical tree, eaten as a nut, so it is an edible fruit.

clue.text: Husband admitting love for Italian wine

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the next piece goes inside

blocks.note: to husband resources is to save them
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A man confesses his love for an Italian white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' looks like a noun; it is the verb meaning to conserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Soave is a dry white wine from the Veneto region of Italy.

clue.text: Sponger left separately, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or said, so the spoken form is what counts

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
each, as in 'a pound each', means separately

explanation.surface: A freeloader departed on their own, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, the letter L and the word for separately sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a bloodsucking worm, and by extension a person who lives off others, a parasite or sponger.

clue.text: Join a navy? I may have

definitions.text: Join a navy? I may have

blocks.note: surface reading: a question about enlisting
setter's reading: the speaker is a sailor who might have done just that

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether to enlist answers that they might have.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the 'I' speaking: a sailor is someone who may well have joined a navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaman is a sailor, typically a member of a navy below the rank of officer.

clue.text: Speak amusingly about very loud artist producing rubbish

blocks.note: to riff on or about a topic is to improvise jokes on it
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist
ff, fortissimo, is the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A comedian jokes about a noisy painter whose work is trash.
explanation.walkthrough: The artist and the loudness mark come in the reverse of their clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Riff-raff means disreputable people, the dregs of society; rubbish is used in the same scornful sense.

clue.text: Endless finance for entertainment

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to fund is to finance

explanation.surface: Unlimited money for amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: Fun means enjoyment or amusement, which is what entertainment provides.

clue.text: Favour parking by river - could be free

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces are set next to each other
could be suggests one possible form among many, so the letters may be rearranged

blocks.note: P is the sign for parking
R is the abbreviation for river
these four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Choosing a riverside spot because parking might be free.
explanation.definitionFit: To favour one thing is to like it better than others, which is what prefer means as a verb.

clue.text: Hairstyle of son, top dog around family

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the pair of pieces wraps the last one

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
the head is the boss or top dog
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: The haircut a boy gets from the family's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The son and top dog join first and then wrap the family word, which lands between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinhead is a very closely shaved haircut, and also the youth subculture named after it.
